kryptpay: The fork has no frontend at all (program and tests only), so there is no app of its own to host.
predix: The fork's app/ is a Create React App UI with no Anchor or web3 client; it never calls the program, so hosting it would not exercise anything on devnet.
seloongmun: The fork's web/ is the create-solana-dapp counter scaffold (increment/decrement): it never calls draw, imports a ShootingIDL file that does not exist, and its build fails.
mons-dot-rehab: end_game has to be signed by the mons game server, and the client is the mons game itself; neither can be hosted as a static page.
valhalla: The app depends on server-side Next.js API routes and Clockwork/Helius services, so a static export cannot run its flow.
elyse: A static site. Its only Solana write, the token faucet, runs server-side with a sender key fetched from the author's own server; the swap page embeds Jupiter Terminal, which is mainnet-only. Nothing here can be proven on devnet without that server.
solstage-web: The app never calls its program's instructions: it uploads the filter file to Shadow Drive (mainnet-only, paid in SHDW) and then tags a PDA of program STAGYb3H… with a memo transaction. That program exists on devnet (deployed by the original author), but the flow cannot complete without a mainnet Shadow Drive upload.
stealthfolio: Swaps go through Jupiter (mainnet-only) and private trades need the Light Protocol relayer server in relayer/; there is no program of its own to deploy.
gluon-solana: Its fission/fusion instructions read a Pyth PriceUpdateV2 account no older than 60 s, and the app posts that update from Pyth Hermes; hermes.pyth.network now answers 401 without an API key, so the flow cannot run from a static page.
decentralogistics: The frontend reads and writes logistics requests through its own Express API server (api-server/, http://localhost:3000), which a static host cannot serve.
solassets-solanahackathon: The app creates its Supabase client at import time from VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (not in the repo), and the Tokens page reads the signed-in Supabase user before calling create_standard_token, so it cannot run without the author's Supabase project.
blocqfinance-colosseum: The Next.js app logs in and loads letters of credit through its own backend (blocq-backend, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL); the program calls (fund, release, refund) are only reachable after that backend's auth.
tagin-solana: The frontends call local Flask/Express APIs (localhost:5000 / 5002) for products and reports.
vv-solana: The client is a MUD (Lattice) game: it boots against EVM world contracts on BSC and a gRPC indexer (VITE_WORLD_CONTRACT, VITE_GRPC_URL, ...) and Particle Network login, and it imports the program IDL from an uncommitted build artifact; the Solana program is only a side module.
gifter-escrow: Every token list and balance in the app comes from Helius DAS calls (getAssetsByOwner, getAssetBatch) to devnet.helius-rpc.com with the author's API key hard-coded in the source; we don't use someone else's key, and the public devnet RPC has no DAS methods.
autohero: The web app's story and hero flow goes through the author's backend API (VITE_API_URL via axios) before it touches the program.
